Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants

No non-solicit on Customer.

Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

[
  "Customer has no non-solicitation restriction."
]

  "The non-solicitation restriction is mutual.",
  "The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.",
  "The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.",
  "General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.",
  "Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.",
  "The restriction does not prohibit hiring."

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The restriction covers only a named competing product.",
  "The restriction applies during the term only.",
  "The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.",
  "The restriction permits Customer's internal development.",
  "The restriction permits Customer acquisitions."
]

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.",
  "The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.",
  "The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.",
  "Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.",
  "Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.",
  "The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.",
  "The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.",
  "The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.",
  "Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.",
  "The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.",
  "Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.",
  "Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.",
  "Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees."
]

[{"id":"sec-p0000","heading":"MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-1","number":"1","heading":"DEFINITIONS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.1","number":"1.1","heading":"“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.2","number":"1.2","heading":"“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.3","number":"1.3","heading":"“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.4","number":"1.4","heading":"“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.5","number":"1.5","heading":"“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.6","number":"1.6","heading":"“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.7","number":"1.7","heading":"“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.8","number":"1.8","heading":"“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2","number":"2","heading":"AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.1","number":"2.1","heading":"Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.2","number":"2.2","heading":"Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.3","number":"2.3","heading":"Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3","number":"3","heading":"SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3.1","number":"3.1","heading":"Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4","number":"4","heading":"ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4.1","number":"4.1","heading":"An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5","number":"5","heading":"IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5.1","number":"5.1","heading":"Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7","number":"7","heading":"FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.1","number":"7.1","heading":"Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2","number":"7.2","heading":"Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2-2","number":"7.2","heading":"Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4-2","number":"12.4","heading":"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.2","number":"24.2","heading":"Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25","number":"25","heading":"PUBLICITY AND MARKS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25.1","number":"25.1","heading":"Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26","number":"26","heading":"COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.1","number":"26.1","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.2","number":"26.2","heading":"Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.4","number":"26.4","heading":"Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27","number":"27","heading":"FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.1","number":"27.1","heading":"Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.2","number":"27.2","heading":"Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.3","number":"27.3","heading":"If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28","number":"28","heading":"GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.1","number":"28.1","heading":"This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.2","number":"28.2","heading":"The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give Vendor written notice of the claim, Vendor shall control its defence and settlement, and Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation. Any indemnity given by Customer under this Agreement is limited to third-party claims arising from content Customer provides to Vendor and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position on all material terms. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual") and is set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. "Fees" (1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees under Order Forms, so the basis is meaningful rather than illusory. 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually ("neither Party is liable"), and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs are direct damages. 21.3 puts confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP wholly outside the cap, with no indemnity sub-cap anywhere else in the document (19.4/19.5 preserve rather than limit those remedies). 21.4 is standard savings language and does not cut back the carve-outs. One point short of the ideal preferred wording, noted but not redlined: the payment carve-out in 21.3 reaches "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all Customer amounts due (Fees excludes taxes, expenses and interest). That is a minor sub-element and does not affect the fallback, every element of which is met.
